loops.name: Senior People Partner · Meridian Health · Round 2
loops.detail: Dana Okafor + one more · 45 min · Google Meet
likelyOpeners: Tell me about a time you handled a difficult employee relations case

stories.title: Warehouse harassment investigation, Q2
stories.body: Two complainants, one long-tenured supervisor, and a site that assumed nothing would happen. I ran eleven interviews in five days, kept both complainants working through schedule changes instead of suspensions, and the termination stood up — no grievance, no appeal.

stories.title: 40-role restructure, two provinces
stories.body: Legal wanted paper speed; managers wanted it over. I sequenced every notification into one day, trained each manager on the script the week before, and redeployed a third of the affected people internally before notice went out.

stories.title: Call-centre onboarding rebuild
stories.body: Ninety-day attrition in the call centre was sitting at 31%. I rebuilt week one around shadowing, moved the compliance modules out of day one, and paired every hire with a floor mentor. Attrition fell to 19% inside two quarters.

answers.question: Tell me about a time you handled a difficult employee relations case.

points.text: Start with the risk: two complainants, one supervisor, a site used to silence
Separate the people, not the payroll — schedule changes, no suspensions
Eleven interviews in five days, documented as I went
The decision stood up — no grievance, no appeal

answers.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a leader and changed the outcome.

points.text: Frame it as a risk disagreement, not a personality one
I brought a sequencing plan, not an objection
Say out loud where I was partly wrong
Land on the relationship after, not the win

answers.question: Tell me about a mistake that had real consequences.

points.text: Own it in one sentence — no wind-up
The first rollout skipped the night shift entirely
What changed: every pilot now names who it excludes

answers.question: How do you handle several urgent cases at once?

points.text: Triage by legal exposure first, people risk second
One case owner per file — no shared inboxes
Tell the waiting managers when, not just that, I'll get to them
Pick the one who controls the outcome, not the loudest
Move the fight to data they already trust
Agree the escalation path before you need it

answers.question: Walk me through how you run a harassment investigation.

points.text: Scope and interim measures in the first 24 hours
Interview order: complainant, witnesses, respondent last
Credibility calls on the record, not in my head
Close the loop with both sides — silence reads as cover-up

answers.question: An employee raises a harassment complaint but asks you not to investigate — what would you do?

points.text: No absolute promises — explain the duty to act on what I now know
Assess severity first: a one-off comment and a pattern take different paths
Agree what happens next and when, so nothing drifts

answers.question: An employee says their manager is retaliating — what do the first 48 hours look like?

points.text: Freeze anything that could look like reprisal — shifts, reviews, access
Get the timeline in their words before memories move
Loop legal early if there's a protected complaint underneath

answers.question: How do you coach a manager who's burning out their team?

points.text: Show them their own attrition and overtime numbers first
Coach the behaviour, not the intention
Set a review date — coaching without a checkpoint is a hope

answers.question: Tell me about a termination that didn't go to plan.

points.text: The plan survived until the room did something human
Security-escort optics cost us that site's trust for a quarter
Now I rehearse the worst five minutes, not the paperwork

answers.question: How do you keep managers compliant across provinces?

points.text: One national floor with provincial overlays — never ten policies
Train on scenarios, not statutes
Audit the exceptions log quarterly — that's where drift shows

answers.question: Tell me about rolling out a policy people hated.

points.text: Name the cost honestly on day one
Give managers the why in their numbers, not HR's
Publish the exception path — pressure needs a valve

answers.question: What would you do if leadership asked you to bend a policy?
triggerPhrases: asked to look the other way

points.text: Clarify what's actually being asked before reacting
Separate legal lines from policy preferences
Offer the compliant version of the same outcome
Document the ask either way
Healthcare scale plus in-house ER — the problems I want
The onboarding rebuild is the work I want to do more of
Ask what the first 90 days need — make it a dialogue

answers.question: Where do you want to take your HR career?

points.text: Towards owning ER strategy, not just the cases
Keep one hand in the messy work — credibility comes from files
Building managers who don't need me is the goal
